issues.description: The solution's PersonResource class has an incorrect constructor signature and body: it accepts a NoteService parameter and sets this.personService = null. This contradicts the problem specification (which expects endpoints in PersonResource that delegate to a functioning PersonService) and prevents Spring from injecting the required PersonService. As a result, any endpoint implementations in PersonResource that call personService (e.g. getAllPersons, createPerson, updatePerson, deletePerson) will throw a NullPointerException at runtime and the solution will not run as intended. This is an unintentional structural error in the solution repository that will confuse students who compare the template, problem statement, and the provided solution.
issues.suggested_fix: Change the PersonResource constructor in the solution to accept a PersonService and assign it to the field. For example: public PersonResource(PersonService personService) { this.personService = personService; } Remove the incorrect NoteService parameter and the null assignment. This aligns the solution with the problem statement and allows Spring to inject the correct service so the endpoints work.

issues.description: Constructor parameter/type mismatch in the solution's PersonResource: the Problem Statement and Template expect PersonResource to be constructed with a PersonService (injected) so the resource can forward person-related requests to the business layer. In the Solution repository PersonResource constructor incorrectly takes a NoteService parameter and sets the personService field to null. This renames/changes the expected service type for the same conceptual entity (the Person service) and breaks the mapping between the problem requirements, the template, and the solution — students comparing artifacts will be confused about which service should be injected and used.
